chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: Playing in the Katherine Dunham show
summary: His group plays the Dunham revue in two theaters; he records transcriptions with Brad Gowans and buys a house in Dumont, New Jersey.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yes. Well, we were a great success with the Katherine Dunham Show and when that show closed, we went from there to another theater; see, her contract ran out in that theater and, then, we went to the--- another theater that was on - was it 48th or 49th-- I can't just remember the theater----
But, I remember, you know, Katherine Dunham dance barefoot---

Yeah - I know -- that's what I'm just about to tell you - that when she went in and saw the second theater and that stage - it had been ripped up by all kinds of heavy stuff and she had men come in and sand that floor down -- the whole stage had to be sanded down. And, of course, now I'm there and I'm very happy and I loved it and I'm doing lots of things with Brad -- making World transcriptions---
Were you doing the same kind of music for that show as you were in Nick's---

Oh, sure -- you know, "The Georgia Cake-walk" which she did a dance to and, uh, "take me to that land of jazz" -- those kind of songs - youknow--- so, I was very happy there and, at that point, I had moved out to New Jersey-- I bought myself a house in New Jersey, in Dumont--- and I was home having breakfast one morning and I got that lovely little thing from the Government - saying you are now drafted into the United States Army and, uh, thinking--- as a matter of fact, I did a Commodore record-an all-night session the
